content.text:
I submitted index 70 (Bi 0.08, Cu 0.51, V 0.41). At 8.5e-7 A it had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured. That's all the merit budget; most of the library wasn't measured, so a better composition could still be in there.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 53 | 0.40 / 0.17 / 0.43 | 4.0e-7 |
| **70** | **0.08 / 0.51 / 0.41** | **8.5e-7** |
| 69 | 0.07 / 0.54 / 0.39 | 6.2e-7 |

- **Why these three:** I started with #53 because it was the closest the library gets to BiVO₄, the standard photoanode for 2.4 eV light. I then tried the Cu–V-rich, low-Bi region, where copper vanadates also absorb at that energy. That point, #70, gave about twice the photocurrent of #53.
- **Last measurement:** #69 has a little more Cu than #70 and came out lower. So along that line the best point is at or near #70, though I didn't test in the other directions around it.
- **Not explored:** I didn't measure the Cu-rich, low-V group (roughly indices 71–136) or the V-rich compositions.
- **Other tools:** The Gaussian-process suggestions weren't useful after only one measurement. I took one XRD pattern of #70 but didn't identify its phase: the phase list was too long to return and I had no way to read the saved file. The choice rests on the photocurrent numbers alone.
